memory_update.text: SABR is the highest direct US-listed pure-play mapping to travel distribution infrastructure, but must be treated as small-cap/high-leverage and transaction-sensitive rather than clean SaaS.
AGYS is a strong underfollowed hospitality software candidate for PMS/POS/payments operations exposure; next layer should verify recurring revenue quality, property expansion, and payment attach.
FOUR is an indirect second-order travel/hospitality infrastructure candidate via payment volume and vertical software, but its node purity is weaker than SABR or AGYS.

PROS would have been a relevant airline pricing/revenue-management software candidate, but it is no longer US-listed after the December 9, 2025 Thoma Bravo acquisition and should be tracked only as private-market validation for the node.
GBTG remains listed as of June 15, 2026 but has a definitive take-private agreement; include only as reference/context unless the deal fails or spread analysis is specifically requested.

node: Travel distribution, hotel operations, channel management, pricing, and payments software
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the travel distribution and operations software node. The best US-listed underfollowed lane currently clusters around Sabre as travel distribution infrastructure, Agilysys as hospitality property/POS/payments software, Shift4 as vertical payments for hospitality/leisure venues, and GBTG as corporate travel platform exposure with a pending take-private overhang. PROS would have been a high-relevance airline revenue-management software candidate, but it ceased trading and was delisted after the Thoma Bravo acquisition completed on December 9, 2025, so it is excluded from candidates.
